uart_api.h

Initialize one UART instance and provide polling character transmit, receive, and initialization-state helpers.

uart_init
int uart_init(
uint32_t 
instance,
uint32_t 
baudrate,
uint32_t 
clock_freq
)

Initializes one UART instance for the bare-metal console path.

Agilex5 and Agilex3 OCRAM builds configure the port using baudrate and clock_freq. DDR builds retain the earlier firmware's UART configuration; both arguments are ignored by those platform initialization hooks.

Parameters
instance
uint32_t

UART instance index. The value must be smaller than UART_MAX_INSTANCE for the selected platform.

baudrate
uint32_t

Requested UART baud rate.

clock_freq
uint32_t

UART input clock frequency in hertz.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL when the instance index is out of range.

uart_deinit
int32_t uart_deinit(
void
)

Disables the active console UART and clears the API's initialized state.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the UART API is not initialized.

uart_is_initialized
bool uart_is_initialized(
void
)

Reports whether the UART API has been initialized.

Returns

true after a successful uart_init(); false otherwise.

uart_putc
void uart_putc(
char 
c
)

Writes one character to the active console UART. If the UART API is not initialized, the call returns without transmitting data. Otherwise it waits for transmit FIFO space; there is no timeout. A newline is sent as CRLF.

Parameters
c
char

Character to transmit.

uart_getc
char uart_getc(
void
)

Reads one character from the active console UART. If the UART API is not initialized, the function returns the NUL character ('\0'). After initialization, it polls until a byte arrives and can block indefinitely.  There is no receive timeout or 'no byte available' return. Check uart_is_initialized() before using a returned NUL as received data.

Returns

The received character, or '\0' when the UART API is not initialized.

printf
int printf(
const 
char 
*
fmt,
...
)

Formats text with the repository's lightweight printf implementation and sends it to the active console UART.

Parameters
fmt
const char*

Format string.

...

Values referenced by the format string.

Returns

The character count produced by the lightweight formatter, even if the UART is uninitialized and drops the output. This is not an errno status or confirmation of delivery to the terminal.
